Choice: Deduplicate in staging: keep one row per loadsmart_id (stg_loads uses DISTINCT ON). Keep dup_id_flag and dup_id_copies on the kept row for audit (staging and intermediate only; they are not columns of fact_load).
Comment: No tie-breaker rule is needed: the duplicated rows are identical in every column and there is no load-system / ingestion timestamp column to choose a version from. The warn test proves the copies really are identical, so the arbitrary pick is harmless.
Test Created: stg_loads.loadsmart_id unique + not_null (error); assert_duplicate_ids_identical (warn, compares the whole raw row and returns ids whose copies differ); fact_load.loadsmart_id unique + not_null (error)

Choice: Do not move to staging. It is loaded only into raw, renamed has_mobile_app_tracking_1, because Postgres rejects two columns with the same name and \copy is positional.
Comment: Only holds the value False, so it has no analytical value. Kept in raw for lineage. A warn accepted_values test [false] is attached to the source column (_staging_sources.yml) only to detect a True value if one ever appears.

Choice: Do not move to the fact table. Dropped from fact: has_mobile_app_tracking, has_macropoint_tracking, has_edi_tracking, contracted_load, carrier_on_time_to_pickup, carrier_on_time_to_delivery, carrier_on_time_overall, pickup_appointment_time, delivery_appointment_time. All nine stay in stg_loads (and raw); none is a column of fact_load.
Comment: Two different reasons: (a) constant column, confirmed only for has_mobile_app_tracking (False only), which stays in staging as a documented column; (b) no analytical value or no relation to the business questions. No analysis proves constancy: analysis_zero_null_blank_raw only reports null, zero and blank values.
Test Created: accepted_values [false] (warn) on stg_loads.has_mobile_app_tracking; no test on the other dropped columns.

Choice: Document as a warning for statistical use. Do not block the pipeline and do not impute (except mileage, see below).
Comment: SQL aggregates (avg, median, min, max) ignore NULL, so the effective n can be smaller than the row count. The warning is written in the dbt column descriptions of fact_load (quote_date, book_date, source_date, pickup_date, delivery_date, book_price, source_price, pnl, mileage) and in the fact_load model description (visible in dbt docs). The tests are severity warn so they surface in CI without blocking a deploy.
Test Created: not_null (warn) on fact_load quote_date, book_date, source_date, pickup_date, delivery_date, book_price, source_price, pnl, mileage; analysis_zero_null_blank_raw; analysis_zero_null_blank_fact

Data Quality Exploration: Zero values in book_price, source_price, pnl
Choice: Keep the zeros (they are NOT cast to NULL) and flag them: zero_book_price_flag, zero_source_price_flag, zero_pnl_flag. Loads with a zero price are left out of price analyses through price_analysis_exclude_flag and the <> 0 filter (nonzero_stats macro). carrier_rating is not touched (only in staging).
Comment: In staging book_price, source_price and pnl hold the same values as book_price_raw, source_price_raw and pnl_raw; fact_load has no *_raw columns. Because zeros stay in the columns, an aggregate that does not filter them will include the zeros: analyses must use price_analysis_exclude_flag and <> 0. A legitimate pnl of 0 is kept and flagged like any other zero. pnl_calculated (book_price - source_price) is also in fact_load and is not reliable when a price is 0.
Test Created: accepted_range >= 0 on book_price (warn); not_null (warn) on book_price, source_price, pnl (catches NULL only; zeros are caught by the zero_*_flag columns and analysis_zero_null_blank_fact); assert_pnl_matches_raw (warn, reads pnl_mismatch_flag = reported pnl vs raw book_price - source_price)

Choice: Flag (cancelled_nonzero_price_flag) and exclude from price analyses through price_analysis_exclude_flag. The load stays in fact_load.
Comment: A cancelled load is expected to have zero in every price. The flag is computed in staging on the raw values and carried to fact_load. price_analysis_exclude_flag = cancelled_nonzero_price_flag OR zero_price_active_flag.

Choice: Flag (zero_price_active_flag) and exclude from price analyses through price_analysis_exclude_flag. The load stays in fact_load.
Comment: zero_price_active_flag = non-cancelled load with book_price, source_price or pnl equal to 0. int_price_outlier_bounds and analysis_lane_price_stats leave price_analysis_exclude_flag loads out.

Choice: Do not move to the fact table. Excluded in the intermediate layer with reason pickup_after_delivery.
Comment: Pickup and delivery are the main dates of the model and a wrong value is too risky. The exclusion uses a strict comparison (pickup_date > delivery_date). The staging flag pickup_after_delivery_flag uses the same strict comparison, so equal timestamps are neither flagged nor excluded and stay in the fact. pickup_gt_delivery_flag is an identical copy used by int_loads_unique to set the reason. Excluded rows remain in int_loads_unique for audit.
Test Created: assert_fact_no_pickup_after_delivery (error, guard); analysis_fact_exclusions_by_reason (count of excluded loads per reason); assert_raw_pickup_after_delivery (warn, raw)

Choice: Keep the rows in the fact and flag them in stg_loads: quote_after_book, quote_after_source, book_after_pickup, quote_after_pickup, source_after_pickup, book_after_source, quote_after_delivery, book_after_delivery, source_after_delivery (plus date_order_flag_count in staging and any_date_order_flag in int_loads_unique). The flags are not columns of fact_load.
Comment: Each flag is computed only when both dates are filled; a missing date never raises a flag. All comparisons are strict (>), so equal timestamps are not flagged. The flags live in staging and intermediate so analysts can decide per analysis.
Test Created: No blocking test (flags only); analysis_lane_quality_summary (per lane sums of the flags and of the zero entries, over loads in fact_load; 'any error' = any zero entry or any date-order flag)

Choice: Do not move to the fact table. The columns stay in stg_loads: carrier_on_time_to_pickup, carrier_on_time_to_delivery, carrier_on_time_overall, pickup_appointment_time, delivery_appointment_time.
Comment: Columns referring to pickup and delivery date appointment and its related booleans present too many inconsistencies.

Choice: Create flag only (never change or remove values), ask the user, keep for analysis by default. Rule: value below the 1st or above the 99th percentile of the non-zero values, for book_price, source_price and pnl.
Comment: Global percentiles (not per lane, where samples would be too small), computed with percentile_cont on the non-zero values of the loads that are in fact_load and are not price_analysis_exclude_flag, so suspicious rows do not move the bounds. Bounds are stored in int_price_outlier_bounds; quantiles are dbt vars declared in dbt_project.yml (outlier_lower_quantile 0.01, outlier_upper_quantile 0.99). Flags in fact_load: book_price_outlier_flag, source_price_outlier_flag, pnl_outlier_flag (there is no combined flag). Zeros and NULLs are never flagged (explicit <> 0 condition in fact_load). When an AI assistant is about to average a price metric it must ask the user whether to include or exclude outliers (default include; rule written in the fact_load ai_hint); the answer is applied with the outliers_mode var (include | exclude) or by filtering on the metric flag, and the choice is stated in the result. analysis_lane_price_stats applies outliers_mode through the outlier_clause macro (book_per_mile uses the book_price flag).
Test Created: assert_price_outlier_bounds_valid (error); assert_outlier_flags_ignore_zero_null (error); assert_price_outlier_rate (warn, expects about 2% flagged per metric, warns at 0% or above 4% (var outlier_rate_warn_max)); analysis_price_outliers (bounds and flagged rows); analysis_lane_price_stats (respects outliers_mode)

Choice: Do not move to the fact table. Excluded in the intermediate layer with reason lane_format_invalid.
Comment: Expected format is "City,ST -> City,ST". lane_format_invalid_flag is raised when the ' -> ' separator is missing, a city is empty or contains a digit, or a state is not two letters (states are upper-cased before the check, so lower-case states are accepted and normalised); a missing lane also counts as invalid.
Test Created: assert_lane_format (error, guard on fact_load + dim_lane); assert_raw_lane_format (warn, raw); analysis_fact_exclusions_by_reason

Choice: Populate with the lane median when the load is not cancelled (load_was_cancelled = false). The median uses only non-cancelled loads of the same lane with mileage > 0.
Comment: Original value kept in mileage_raw (intermediate only; fact_load has the imputed mileage); mileage_imputed_flag marks filled rows and mileage_unresolved_flag marks lanes with no other value to use (mileage stays 0 and must be ignored in statistics); zero_mileage_flag (raw 0) is also in fact_load. Cancelled loads with mileage 0 are not imputed. Mileage 0 or NULL must not enter averages or medians (book_price_per_mile is NULL in that case).
Test Created: assert_fact_zero_mileage (warn, lists remaining 0 or NULL mileage rows); analysis_lane_quality_summary (zero, imputed and unresolved counts per lane)

Choice: Warn and analyze only; no row is changed or removed.
Comment: A lane should have one distance. When the spread (max - min) of non-zero mileage of non-cancelled loads is above 100 miles the lane is listed with its distinct values and their frequencies. The dbt test and analysis read fact_load (mileage already imputed); the script reads the raw data. The threshold is the dbt var mileage_spread_threshold (dbt_project.yml).
Test Created: assert_lane_mileage_spread (warn); analysis_lane_mileage_multiple_values; scripts/lane_mileage_inconsistency.py (pandas version on raw)

Data Quality Exploration: Reported pnl differs from book_price - source_price (added)
Comment: Computed on the raw values in staging (zeros are kept, so raw and model values are the same). The test reads pnl_mismatch_flag, so it compares the reported pnl with the raw difference.

Choice: Keep the load in fact_load. equipment_id is never NULL: it is the surrogate hash of NULL and has no row in dim_equipment (dim_equipment skips NULL equipment_type).
Comment: Documented in the fact_load column description so analysts do not expect a NULL key.

Choice: fact_load also carries: pnl_calculated, book_price_per_mile, is_delivered, zero_entry_count, zero_mileage_flag and price_analysis_exclude_flag.
Comment: pnl_calculated = book_price - source_price; book_price_per_mile = book_price / mileage (NULL when book_price is NULL or mileage is 0 or NULL); is_delivered = not cancelled (not 'has a delivery date'); zero_entry_count = how many of the four zero flags are true.
